title: The `[debug] mode` key parses and is read by nothing, so a value written there turns on no probe.
text: `rule:testing/debug-mode-directive` states `[debug] mode` as a default and a ceiling for the debug probes. The probes are compiled into every unit and `nvs_runtime`'s `DebugFlags` arms them, but nothing turns a bit on from the file and the directive registry has no row for this key (`crates/nvs-config/src/tree.rs:514-519`), so a coverage run configured there never starts. The mechanical half is a `RuntimeTighten`/`Reload` row, a boot refusal of a name outside the four, and `nvs_runtime::Ctx::set_config` arming the named bits and dropping the ones the previous snapshot armed. A request cannot set the key, because a list is not a quantity (`crates/nvs-config/src/request.rs:28`). **The user decided the served case:** `nvs run` and `nvs test` arm the bits the file names, and a server whose `[debug] mode` names any bit fails its boot with an error that says why, the same on every platform, and `rule:testing/debug-mode-directive` says so. The reasons: `DebugFlags::TRACE` makes `Ctx::record_trace` push two owned `String` events per compiled call (`crates/nvs-runtime/src/ctx/trace.rs:305`), with no ceiling (`SPAN_EVENT_CEILING` exempts that bit), and nothing reads `call` events of a served request: `nvs_server::trace` drops the kind, and `rule:observability/four-kinds-become-a-span` refuses that cost on a served request. Whether the per-request allocator charges those strings is not checked. `coverage` and `branch` count into a `StmtHits` table, and a served request has none, so they count nothing. Arming the bits on a server with a cap on its `call` events was declined because it is a new limit, and refusing only `trace` and `profile` because `coverage` and `branch` would be accepted and do nothing. Coverage of a live server is its own feature, not designed.
